title: Smooth and intrinsic comparison of finite normalized-word histories
statement:
Over $\mathbf Q$, consider closed embeddings $X\hookrightarrow P$ with $X$ reduced and $P$ smooth, separated and of finite type [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix the normalized word assignment of [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]: $w_H=\bot$ on regular points and $w_H(x)=(A_x,t_x)$ on singular points, with normalized head $A_x=(c_x,\Delta^{q_x}h_x)$ and the tail of the marked-ideal word of a minimal-envelope Hilbert--Samuel presentation. Use its finite admissible histories, retaining the ordered inverse images of earlier center ideals even when the intrinsic blowup is an identity [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history].

Here a smooth ambient pullback starts with a smooth morphism $Q\to P$, where $Q$ is separated and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and the cartesian pair $Y=X\times_P Q\hookrightarrow Q$. For a cartesian smooth ambient pullback of such a finite history, the pulled-back history exists with precisely the empty-center stages deleted. Its ambient schemes are again smooth, separated and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and its strict transforms are reduced. If $y$ corresponds to $x$ at a retained stage, then $w(y)=w(x)$, without a constant-relative-dimension hypothesis. In terms of the local head, if $s$ is the dimension of the local ring of the smooth fibre at $y$, then $h_y=\Lambda^s h_x$, $q_y=q_x+s$ and $c_y=c_x$; the marked-ideal tails also agree. For any full maximum stratum of the original stage, the extension of its reduced defining ideal to the pulled-back strict transform is the reduced ideal of its inverse-image stratum; this is the unit ideal if that stratum is empty. The same ideal equality holds in the ambient schemes. This statement concerns an individual stratum even when its inverse image is not a maximum stratum of the whole pulled-back scheme.

If two finite histories have isomorphic strict-transform diagrams over an isomorphism of the initial reduced schemes, preserving all earlier center ideals and their order, hence the induced exceptional birth-stage data, the identified functions $w_H$ agree, in their common value space, and so do the reduced ideals of their maximum strata on the strict transforms. This comparison allows different smooth ambient embeddings. All these equalities commute with open restriction and further smooth pullback of the histories.

proof.text: Induct on the generators of admissible histories in [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history], retaining as inductive assertions that every ambient stage is smooth, separated and finite type over $\mathbf Q$, every strict transform is reduced, and every actual center is smooth and closed in its ambient stage. The empty history has the given properties. For a maximum extension, [lem-trf-resolution-word-maximum-center-descent] makes the center regular with coherent defining ideals. It is of finite type by [lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type], applied with the closed subset of $P_H$ and $U=P_H$; it is smooth over the perfect field $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-center-blowup-geometry] to obtain the next ambient scheme and the reduced strict transform. The smooth-comparison generator is handled by the finite base-change construction in step 2. This is induction on the construction of a finite history, not an assumption of termination.

proof.text: For a history satisfying the inductive assertions, pull back its successive stages along $Q\to P$. Smoothness implies flatness by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], so each ambient square is cartesian and each comparison is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The generic-component hypothesis of [lem-trf-strict-transform-flat-etale-base-change] holds: on affine charts flat going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] implies that a minimal prime upstairs contracts to a minimal prime downstairs (a strictly smaller contracted prime would lift below it). That node therefore identifies the strict transforms scheme-theoretically. Every pulled-back center is smooth over $\mathbf Q$, by smooth base change and composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. The initial $Y$ is reduced: $X$ is finite type over the Noetherian field $\mathbf Q$, hence locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the smooth map has geometrically reduced fibres by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], so [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback] applies. Starting with this pair in $Q$, apply [lem-trf-smooth-center-blowup-geometry] at each stage, giving all the required geometry and reducedness. If the extended center ideal is the unit ideal, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] makes the entire stage an identity. Delete just those stages; every other center is nonempty. This supplies precisely the smooth-comparison generator of [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history] and completes the induction in step 1.

proof.text: At corresponding points $y\mapsto x$ of any cartesian stage, [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile] gives $h_y=\Lambda^s h_x$, $q_y=q_x+s$ and $c_y=c_x$, where $s$ is the local fibre dimension at this particular $y$. Since $\Delta\Lambda f=f$ (subtract successive partial sums, including the value at zero), $\Delta^{q_y}h_y=\Delta^{q_x+s}\Lambda^s h_x=\Delta^{q_x}h_x$. Thus the heads agree. The same node says the regular head occurs exactly at regular points, so regularity is equivalent at these corresponding points. Both words are then $\bot$, or both are singular words. No global choice of $s$ or constant relative dimension has been used.

proof.text: At a singular point choose the maximal-order, codimension-zero minimal-envelope presentation used by [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]. By [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations] its presentation class commutes with local smooth pullback, with the retained Hilbert--Samuel level summed by the local relative dimension. Consequently the pulled-back presentation represents the prescribed level on the pulled-back scheme, even if a different presentation was chosen there. The numerical engine [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine] gives the same word under smooth pullback; its invariance under test equivalence makes it independent of that replacement. Both leading entries are $1$, so deleting them gives $t_y=t_x$. The history is identified by actual extension of the earlier center ideals in step 2, in their original order. An omitted center extends to the unit ideal, hence creates no exceptional component; its original place is still known. Birth stages of all retained components are therefore identified under the deletion map. Earlier centers whose intrinsic blowup is an identity are retained, as required by [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. Combining this tail equality with step 3 proves $w(y)=w(x)$ in the fixed common value space.

proof.text: Now take an intrinsic comparison of two histories. An isomorphism of the local rings preserves their maximal-ideal powers, lengths and dimensions, so it preserves $h_x,q_x,c_x$ and regularity. At a singular point [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations] identifies the test-equivalence classes in the two minimal envelopes using precisely the intrinsic transformed scheme, the retained level and the ordered earlier center ideals. The minimal envelopes have the same support dimension: their cotangent spaces are those of the identified intrinsic germ. The test-equivalence clause of [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine], with these identified ordered histories and equal support dimensions, identifies the tails. [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing] permits these local presentation computations to compute the prescribed global words in their common value space. Thus the two words agree everywhere. In particular their maximum loci correspond as subsets, including the empty case. This argument uses no identification of the original ambient schemes and discards no earlier ideal when its blowup happens to be an identity.

proof.text: Let $T$ be a full maximum stratum at a stage. It is closed by [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]. Its reduced closed subscheme $M$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The closed stratum $M$ is finite type over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type], with ambient $P_H$ and $U=P_H$, and is locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For the smooth comparison $g$ of step 2, smooth morphisms are flat [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and have geometrically reduced fibres [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Hence $M\times g$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback]. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-flat-pullback-recognition] first to $M\hookrightarrow X_H$ and then to $M\hookrightarrow P_H$: in both cases the extended ideal is exactly the reduced ideal of the inverse-image subset. This applies to an individual original $T$, irrespective of whether it becomes a full maximum after pullback. If the inverse image is empty its ideal is the unit ideal, by the vanishing-ideal formula. For the intrinsic isomorphism in step 5, uniqueness of the reduced induced structure in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] similarly identifies the intrinsic maximum ideals.

proof.text: All value equalities above are pointwise equalities in the one word space, so restriction or a further smooth comparison gives the same equality by transitivity. For ideals, extending an ideal generated locally by sections $a_i$ first along $g$ and then along $h$ gives the ideal generated by $h^*g^*a_i=(g\circ h)^*a_i$, exactly direct extension. [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history] retains that ordered list under comparisons; successive deletions omit exactly the stages whose final extended ideal is the unit ideal. A stage already omitted remains unit after further extension, and any newly missed center is now omitted. Thus the retained order and birth-stage identifications are the same for composite and successive pullback. Open restriction is a smooth comparison by the same definition. This proves all the claimed compatibility equalities, also for empty schemes, length-zero histories and a pullback missing every center.
